newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends sharply higher on low heat stocks.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends sharply higher on low heat stocks.

text.p: IPE Dec Brent closed near its contract high on continued concerns over low distillate stocks, traders said, even as the U.S. Energy Secretary was going to see if the U.S. industry can pump out more heating oil.
But traders said worries over political instability in Russia and skirmishes in Iraq had discouraged the bears ahead of the weekend and had already helped reignite the three-month-old bull market.
Secretary Hazel O'Leary told reporters in Washington before she went into a meeting with 14 top executives that she would whether they had extra capacity in their refineries.
She also said she was going to ask the executives to explain how long they expected Europe to be an attractive market for heating oil exports. The news came out as the markets closed.

"The gas oil finished very strong in the nearby contracts and it could be concerned over the heating oil stocks in the U.S. that is highlighted by this meeting," a broker said, explaining crude's rally.
He said any efforts to limit heating oil exports out of the U.S., as some speculated, would do little to puncture the strong market in Europe.
"In the whole global complex we're talking about the same barrel of oil whether it's in the Med or in the Northeast U.S.," he said.
Dec Brent last traded up 36 cents at $24.55 a barrel after coming within one cent of its contract high of $24.60.
The spot Brent contract reached a post-Gulf War high this week of $25.06 to punctuate a rally that started below $19 in late July.
Nov gas oil earlier jumped $6.25 to close at $233.75 a tonne.

The broker warned that gas oil prices may pull back early next week, however, due to warmer temperatures expected for northwest Europe this weekend and because of a wave of cargoes arriving from North America.
